findings.title: NPE risk in hasPermission when 'Clients' aggregate resource is missing
findings.body: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when resourceStore.findByName returns null, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...).getResourceTypeResource can legitimately return null (it does so when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false, or when the resource for the type is missing). The very next line calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) with that potentially null resource, which throws NullPointerException. The fallback path must null-check resource before calling findByResource (or simply return false if no 'Clients' aggregate resource exists), otherwise a missing resource will crash permission evaluation in production.

findings.title: Listener gated on V1 feature flag will skip V2 cleanup
findings.body: registerListener now wraps all event handlers in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`. ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is the V1 flag; V2 is gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 elsewhere (in evaluator()/management()). If only the V2 flag is enabled, the listener body never runs, so RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent will no longer trigger setPermissionsEnabled(...) cleanup on the corresponding permission resources. The original code ran unconditionally and let management() route to V1 or V2. Either the check should be `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ || ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` (or just the V2 flag), or the V2 implementations must actually be wired up so these events still get processed.

findings.title: ClientRemovedEvent handler will throw UnsupportedOperationException in V2
findings.body: The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. When the V2 profile feature is on, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled is implemented as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. The same goes for the role/group branches (no V2 implementation shown). So if the listener ever runs in V2 mode, it will propagate an UnsupportedOperationException out of the KeycloakSession event manager, surfacing as a 500/error during client/role/group deletion. Either the V2 implementations must provide real setPermissionsEnabled behavior, or the listener must explicitly skip V2 (the inverse of the bug above).

findings.title: requireView / requireViewClientScopes Javadoc claims a return value
findings.body: The newly-added Javadoc on requireView (around line 95) and requireViewClientScopes (around line 100) both start with "Returns {@code true} if ..." but the methods themselves return void (they throw ForbiddenException on failure). The Javadoc is wrong/misleading; it should describe that the method throws ForbiddenException when the corresponding canXxx() check is false, matching the style already used for requireManage, requireList, etc.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission leaks the 'Clients' aggregate name into the result
findings.body: resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...) returns every resource whose type is "Clients" — that includes both per-client resources (named by client.getId()) and the schema's aggregate 'all-clients' resource (named "Clients"). The lambda then does `granted.add(resource.getName())`. When the caller has an all-clients permission that matches the requested scope, the string "Clients" ends up in the returned Set, mixed in with actual client UUIDs. Callers using this set (e.g., to filter what a user can manage or to look up clients by ID) will see a phantom "Clients" entry. The aggregate resource should be skipped (or its name normalized out) so only concrete client IDs are returned.

findings.title: Unused private method and dead imports
findings.body: getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is defined but never called from anywhere in the class (canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, and no other call site uses it). The static import `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` and the import `org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope` are likewise unused. These should be removed, or the helper should be wired into the permission evaluation if it is intended to provide kc.client.id attributes for policies.

findings.title: findByName uses raw client.getId() with no null/empty guard
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())` is called without verifying that client.getId() is non-null and non-empty. If the ClientModel has not been persisted yet (transient client during creation) or has been removed between the caller fetching it and this check, client.getId() can be null/blank, and the lookup will silently match a resource with an empty/null name (the all-resource aggregate has the name "Clients", but the default-find semantics for blank keys are implementation-defined). Guarding the lookup with a null check on client.getId() would prevent surprising false positives/negatives.
